name: WXImpactBench
description: Climate change adaptation requires the understanding of disruptive weather impacts on society, where large language models (LLMs) might be applicable. However, their effectiveness is under-explored due to the difficulty of high-quality corpus collection and the lack of available benchmarks. The climate-related events stored in regional newspapers record how communities adapted and recovered from disasters. However, the processing of the original corpus is non-trivial. In this study, we first develop a disruptive weather impact dataset with a four-stage well-crafted construction pipeline. Then, we propose WXImpactBench, the first benchmark for evaluating the capacity of LLMs on disruptive weather impacts. The benchmark involves two evaluation tasks, multi-label classification and ranking-based question answering. evaluation_method: F1 for multi-label classification and ranking-based QA metrics (e.g., nDCG/MRR or accuracy@k)
reputation: A very recent benchmark proposed for evaluating LLMs on disruptive weather impact understanding, with limited community adoption so far.
notes: New benchmark with likely limited public results and possible dataset-size/coverage constraints; non-LLM text benchmark.
